content.title: Heat vs. Cavaliers: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/27/26)
content.text: The Miami Heat (39–34) face the Cleveland Cavaliers (45–28) tonight at Rocket Arena in Cleveland in their second matchup this week. The Heat took their meeting on Wednesday in a dominant 120–103 win, snapping a five-game losing streak. Norman Powell led a balanced attack with 19 points — one of eight Miami players who scored in double-digits. Tyler Herro scored 18 and Bam Adebayo finished with a 17-point, 10-rebound double-double. Miami shot 52% from the field while holding the Cavs to just 43% shooting. Donovan Mitchell led Cleveland with 28 points. Both he and Sam Merrill knocked down four 3-pointers each. James Harden finished with 18 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists. Wednesday’s defeat ended Cleveland’s win streak at four games. But they enter tonight in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, eight games out of first, but with a comfortable four-game cushion over the Atlanta Hawks. They’re 2.5 games behind the third-place New York Knicks, and an additional game separates them and the second-place Boston Celtics. A move up a spot or two is possible, though not likely. Miami, meanwhile, sits in 10th place in the Eastern Conference, just 1.5 games behind the sixth-place Toronto Raptors. They’re on the verge of clinching a play-in berth at a minimum, but could mount a late push for an automatic playoff spot. Expect the Cavs to bounce back and edge out the Heat to take tonight’s rematch. Prediction: Cleveland Cavaliers 117, Miami Heat 112 Injury Report Miami Heat Jaime Jaquez Jr. — GTD (Ankle) Terry Rozier — Out (Not Injury Related) Cleveland Cavaliers Jarrett Allen — GTD (Knee) Dean Wade — Out (Ankle) Jaylon Tyson — Out (Toe) Craig Porter Jr. — Out (Groin) How to Watch Heat vs. Cavaliers Tip-off for tonight’s Heat-Cavaliers game is set for 7:30 PM Eastern at Rocket Arena in Cleveland.
